title: Ambedkar: Life, Politics and Philosophy
sources_used: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

papers.paper_title: EXAMINATION PAPER 1: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 ADMISSION REGULAR EXAM SEM 4, MARCH 2026

questions.question: Examine the historical context that shaped Ambedkar’s socio-political activism
questions.solution_html:
• Experience marked by Brahmanical dominance, caste oppression, untouchability
  • social exclusion, and unequal access to education and public life. Struggle for reform
  • dignity and political, legal and social rights
questions.final_answer: dignity and political, legal and social rights
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Assess the importance of constitutional safeguards in Ambedkar’s socio-political / framework.
questions.solution_html:
• Constitution as a tool of reform, rights, equality and dignity. Constitution as a tool for
  • protection and upliftment. Inability of social reform alone in dismantling caste- need
  • of legal backing.
questions.final_answer: of legal backing
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Identify the constitutional provisions that prohibit caste-based discrimination.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of Ambedkar in turning constitution as a tool against caste oppression.
  • Fundamental rights- Article 15, 16, 17.
questions.final_answer: Role of Ambedkar in turning constitution as a tool against caste oppression
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List the principal forms of discrimination faced by Dalits under the Brahmanical / order.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of caste in Indian society. Discriminations- untouchability, social segregation
  • restrictions on/ denial of access to public places, denial of education, occupational
  • stigma, dehumanisation, humiliation, social boycott, exclusion form civic and
  • religious institutions.
questions.final_answer: religious institutions
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the ideological differences between Ambedkar and Gandhi regarding / caste reform.
questions.solution_html:
• Ambedkar- rejection of caste and call for its annihilation- caste as structurally rooted
  • in Hindu social order. Gandhi- call for reform within in the Hindu society- emphasis
  • on moral transformation of the oppressor- caste as an evil that can be corrected.
questions.final_answer: on moral transformation of the oppressor- caste as an evil that can be corrected
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What was Ambedkar’s position on the relationship between caste and class?
questions.solution_html:
• The difference in position between Ambedkar and the left. Ambedkar- caste not as a
  • form of class inequality- more rigid, hereditary, and religiously sanctioned system of
  • social division.
questions.final_answer: social division
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Outline Ambedkar’s views on the role of industrialisation in national progress.
questions.solution_html:
• Industrialisation- necessary for economic modernisation, social mobility, and the
  • weakening of caste-based village structures. Role of industries in creating mobile
  • workforce, expanding employment, and reducing dependence on traditional caste
  • occupations.
questions.final_answer: occupations
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the major labour reforms introduced as a result of Ambedkar’s efforts.
questions.solution_html:
• Measures for labour welfare- regulation of working conditions, maternity benefits
  • fixed working hours, labour rights. Ambedkar linked labour welfare with social
  • justice- state as an institution responsible for protecting workers.
  • Short Essay Questions
questions.final_answer: Short Essay Questions
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: How did Ambedkar's legal career intersect with his activism for Dalit rights?
questions.solution_html:
• Legal training as a tool to challenge caste discrimination through legislation, public
  • argument, and constitutional design. Use of legal reasoning to defend rights, logically
  • critique social hierarchy and shape legal protections through the constitution.
questions.final_answer: critique social hierarchy and shape legal protections through the constitution
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyse Ambedkar’s views on labour welfare and workers’ rights.
questions.solution_html:
• Ambedkar and the centrality of labour rights to economic progress and democracy.
  • Economic exploitation and social inequality as mutually reinforcing. State
  • intervention in industry. Call for welfare measures.
questions.final_answer: intervention in industry. Call for welfare measures
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Assess the extent to which independent India has realised the goals envisioned / in 'Annihilation of Caste'
questions.solution_html:
• equal in legal terms- constitutional protections, reservation, civil rights, anti
  • discrimination laws. Areas left unaddressed- law in practice, role of caste in shaping
  • social life, political power, access to resources- violence.
questions.final_answer: social life, political power, access to resources- violence
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Evaluate the political consequences of Ambedkar’s resignation over the stalling / of the Hindu Code Bill.
questions.solution_html:
• Resignation due to slow pace of social reform- unwillingness of dominant political
  • forces to confront patriarchy. Ambedkar's resignation exposed the limits of post
  • independence reformism, stood as a proof of how strong the conservative forces were
  • in an independent India. Highlighted the commitment of Ambedkar towards women’s
  • rights, legal equality, and secular social reform.
questions.final_answer: rights, legal equality, and secular social reform
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Examine how conversion challenged entrenched norms within caste society.
questions.solution_html:
• Ambedkar's conversion to Navayana Buddhism- rejected Hindu ritual hierarchy and
  • spiritual basis of untouchability- questioned caste ridden society and Brahmanical
  • authority- asserted the ability of Dalits to create dignified moral community outside
  • the caste order and claim self-respect through a new religious identity.
questions.final_answer: the caste order and claim self-respect through a new religious identity
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Examine how social democracy forms the foundation of Ambedkar’s nationalism.
questions.solution_html:
• Social democracy- commitment towards Liberty, equality, fraternity and belief in
  • social efficiency through harnessing the maximum potential of an individual.
  • Ambedkar's nationalism- argued for social justice- without social justice nationalism
  • remained hollow and reproduced caste domination and class elites.
questions.final_answer: remained hollow and reproduced caste domination and class elites
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the distinction Ambedkar made between equality of opportunity and / equality of outcome.
questions.solution_html:
• Equality of opportunity- same access to education, jobs, public life etc... Equality of
  • outcome- social and material results being equal. Historical disadvantage. Need for
  • affirmative action.
  • Essay Questions
questions.final_answer: Essay Questions
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Assess the continuing relevance of Ambedkar’s ideas on minorities in / contemporary democratic societies.
questions.solution_html:
• Ambedkar's emphasis on safeguards against majoritarian domination, equal
  • citizenship, constitutional protection, political representation, rights-based democracy
  • and fraternity. Need for inclusion- essential for nation building.
questions.final_answer: and fraternity. Need for inclusion- essential for nation building
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: To what extent does Ambedkar’s critique of caste provide a framework for / achieving social equality?
questions.solution_html:
• Ambedkar's critique of caste- exposed caste as a system of graded inequality- role of
  • religion, endogamy and social power in sustaining the system. Solution- legal rights
  • social reform, education, political representation, moral transformation- equality
  • transformed to a structural goal rather than philosophical.
questions.final_answer: transformed to a structural goal rather than philosophical
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Assess whether Navayana Buddhism provided a sustainable alternative to / caste-based hierarchy.
questions.solution_html:
• Navayana- ethical and political alternative to Brahmanical authority- stress on
  • equality- repurposing of Buddhist ideas to achieve social justice and dignity- new
  • identity to Dalits and their struggles- role in community mobilisation and anti-caste
  • struggle.
questions.final_answer: struggle
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Evaluate whether Ambedkar’s constitutional framework adequately addressed / structural social inequalities.
questions.solution_html:
• addressed institutionalising equality, fundamental rights, abolition of untouchability
  • reservations, and democratic safeguards. But a constitution is as good as those
  • enacting it and following it. Problems with implementation- caste, patriarchy
  • domination by majority and inequality are still realities.
questions.final_answer: domination by majority and inequality are still realities
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
